meaning:
ἀπο-κόπτω
[in LXX for קָצַץ, כָּרַת, etc. ;]
to cut off: Mrk.9:43, 45, Jhn.18:10, 26 Act.27:32. Mid., to mutilate oneself, have oneself mutilated: Gal.5:12 (cf. Deu.23:1 LXX; and see Cremer, 751; MM, see word).†
(AS)

renderings.bsb: they would proceed to emasculate themselves

elsewhere.note: If your hand causes you to stumble, cut it off. It is better for you to enter into life maimed, rather than having your two hands to go into Gehenna, into the…
Simon Peter therefore, having a sword, drew it, struck the high priest’s servant, and cut off his right ear. The servant’s name was Malchus.
Then the soldiers cut away the ropes of the boat, and let it fall off.
I wish that those who disturb you would cut themselves off.
